steps.title: Import Vue and ref from vue
steps.instruction: Import Vue and ref from the 'vue' package to enable reactive state management in your component.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in Vue and ref from the 'vue' module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing from a package
import { ref, computed } from 'vue'
steps.expectedOutcome: The Vue framework and ref function are imported and available for use in your component.
successCriteria: Vue and ref are imported from 'vue'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported Vue and ref. This gives you access to Vue's reactivity system.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both Vue and ref from the 'vue' package.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check your import statement. You need to import both Vue and ref from 'vue'.

steps.title: Create main App component
steps.instruction: Create a Vue component named App with a default export. The component should return a single root element.
steps.hint: Use the Vue component structure with a template that returns a div.
steps.seedCode:
// Import Vue and ref from 'vue'

// Create the App component here
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is defined and exported as the default.
successCriteria: App component is created with a default export and returns a single root div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the main App component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the component is exported as default and has a template with a single root element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component isn't set up correctly. Check the component structure and export.

steps.title: Initialize theme state with ref
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, declare a reactive theme state variable using ref with the default value 'light'.
steps.hint: Use the ref function you imported earlier to create a reactive reference. Name the variable something descriptive like 'theme'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating reactive state
const count = ref(0);
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a reactive theme state variable initialized with 'light' that can be used throughout your component.
successCriteria: A theme state variable is declared using ref with the initial value 'light'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created reactive theme state. This will allow your component to track and update the current theme.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using ref() with the value 'light' to initialize your theme state.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Inside the setup() function, use ref('light') to create a reactive theme state variable.

steps.title: Define toggleTheme handler
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, define a function named toggleTheme that toggles the theme state between 'light' and 'dark'.
steps.hint: You can use an if statement or a ternary operator to check the current theme value and set it to the opposite.
steps.expectedOutcome: A toggleTheme function that switches the theme state between 'light' and 'dark' when called.
successCriteria: The toggleTheme function is defined inside setup and correctly toggles the theme state value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the toggleTheme handler that switches between light and dark themes.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it correctly toggles between 'light' and 'dark' theme values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The toggleTheme function is missing or doesn't properly toggle the theme state. Try checking the current value and setting it to the opposite.

steps.title: Add main container with dynamic class
steps.instruction: In the return object of your setup function, add a main div container with a dynamic class binding that uses the theme state value.
steps.hint: Use Vue's class binding syntax :class to conditionally apply a CSS class based on the theme value. For example, you could bind to a class like 'dark-theme' when theme is 'dark'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The setup function now returns a main div container with a dynamic class that will change based on the theme state.
successCriteria: A main div container is returned with a dynamic class binding that references the theme state value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a main container with dynamic class binding. This will allow your theme to visually change when the theme state updates.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using Vue's class binding syntax (:class) and referencing the theme state value in your binding.
steps.feedbackWrong: The main container with dynamic class binding isn't quite right. Remember to add a div element in the return object and use :class to bind a class based on the theme state.

steps.title: Add header with theme title
steps.instruction: Inside the main container div, add an <h1> header element that displays the current theme value from your theme state.
steps.hint: Use the theme ref's value in the template with double curly braces {{ }} to display the current theme.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: displaying a state value in a header

Current theme: {{ theme }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will show a header displaying the current theme value (initially 'light').
successCriteria: An <h1> element is added inside the main container that displays the current theme value using {{ theme }}.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a header that displays the current theme value.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a header, but make sure it displays the theme value using {{ theme }}.
steps.feedbackWrong: The header isn't displaying the theme value correctly. Check that you're using {{ theme }} inside the <h1> element.

steps.title: Add theme toggle button
steps.instruction: Add a button element inside the main container that calls the toggleTheme function when clicked. The button should have the text 'Toggle Theme'.
steps.hint: Use the @click directive to wire the button's click event to the toggleTheme handler. Place the button after the header element.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a button with click handler
<button @click="handleClick">Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button labeled 'Toggle Theme' appears in the UI that switches between light and dark themes when clicked.
successCriteria: Button element with @click="toggleTheme" and text 'Toggle Theme' is added to the template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the theme toggle button with the correct click handler.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure it has @click="toggleTheme" and the text 'Toggle Theme'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button is missing or doesn't have the correct click handler. Add a button with @click="toggleTheme" and text 'Toggle Theme'.

steps.title: Add component library card
steps.instruction: Inside the template, add a card component with themed styling that responds to theme changes. Use a <div> with a class of 'card' and include a title and description inside.
steps.hint: Add a <div> element with class='card' inside the main container. Inside this div, add a heading and paragraph with themed content.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a themed card component

Card Title

This card adapts to the current theme.
steps.expectedOutcome: A card component with themed styling is added to the UI, demonstrating how component library elements can adapt to theme changes.
successCriteria: A <div> with class='card' is added inside the main container, containing a heading and paragraph with themed content.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a themed card component that will respond to theme changes.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a card, but make sure it has the correct structure with a heading and paragraph inside.
steps.feedbackWrong: The card component wasn't added correctly. Check that you placed a <div> with class='card' inside the main container with appropriate content.

steps.title: Add themed button component
steps.instruction: Create a new component called ThemedButton inside your App component's setup function, which returns a button element with theme-aware styling.
steps.hint: Define a function called ThemedButton that returns a button element. Use the theme value to conditionally apply CSS classes.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a reusable ThemedButton component defined inside your App component's setup function.
successCriteria: The ThemedButton component is defined as a function that returns a button element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a reusable ThemedButton component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a component, but make sure it's named ThemedButton and returns a button element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ThemedButton component isn't properly defined. Create a function called ThemedButton that returns a button element.

steps.title: Add CSS for theme styles
steps.instruction: Add a <style> section at the end of your Vue file with CSS classes for the light and dark theme variants. Define styles for the .light and .dark classes to control background colors, text colors, and button appearances.
steps.hint: Remember that in Vue single-file components, you can add a <style> tag after your template. Use the class names that match your dynamic class binding (theme).
steps.expectedOutcome: The app will have visual theme styles applied through CSS classes, making the light and dark themes visually distinct.
successCriteria: A <style> section is added with CSS rules for .light and .dark classes that define background colors, text colors, and other theme-specific styles.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've successfully added theme-specific CSS styles. The light and dark themes now have distinct visual appearances.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a style section, but make sure you've defined both .light and .dark classes with appropriate CSS properties like background-color and color.
steps.feedbackWrong: The style section is missing or incomplete. Add a <style> tag with CSS rules for both .light and .dark classes to implement the theme styling.
